item.description: U.S. District Court Judge Tanya Chutkin ordered both sides to talk and to agree on a proposed briefing schedule on the motion for a temporary restraining order by Saturday evening.

item.title: What a midterm race in Kentucky says about how Democrats may do in Trump strongholds
item.description: Democrats are putting up a fight in midterm races this year that went for President Donald Trump by double digits in 2024. Kentucky Public Radio's Sylvia Goodman explains what we can learn from one Kentucky district.

item.title: Election officials worry about DOJ monitoring of Tuesday's vote
item.description: Some election officials have been notified that the DOJ will be monitoring their polling stations. NPR's voting correspondent Miles Parks explains what he's watching for on election day - and afterwards.

item.title: The Healthcare Election: Florida
item.description: When federal subsidies for Affordable Care Act health insurance expired last year, Florida was hit particularly hard. Now, as the election and open enrollment coincide, healthcare is a major issue.

item.title: Week in Politics: Trump's Midwest pivot; sharper Democratic messaging
item.description: The president heads to the midwest for two rallies he previously said were cancelled. Has his message changed this campaign season and how have Democrats sharpened their messaging?

item.title: NPR special: 5 takeaways from a year of listening to swing voters
item.description: Every election, there is a crucial sliver of voters who help determine which candidates win. Here are five takeaways from a year of listening to voters who backed Biden in 2020 and then Trump in 2024.
